facts.label: Two D1 databases with different owners
facts.value: DB (accounts, 28 tables) and JOBDATA (collected postings, 19 tables). The job-data migrations contain no user_id column.
facts.how_counted: wrangler.toml binds DB and JOBDATA. grep -c user_id migrations-job-data/*.sql returns 0 for all 9 files. Accounts schema.sql has user_id on the per-person tables. Only lib/collector.js and the owner-only operations routes write JOBDATA; finder.js and catalogue.js read it.

facts.label: Direction of data flow between the databases
facts.value: The finder reads open postings from JOBDATA and writes the account's own rows (jobs, seen, job_extras) into DB.
facts.how_counted: lib/finder.js: JOBDATA.prepare(SELECT ... FROM postings WHERE open=1 ...) for candidates; db.prepare(...) on jobs, seen and meta keyed by user_id for known rows and results.

facts.label: Budget clamp per run
facts.how_counted: effectiveConfig() takes the minimum of the constants and the global, provider and host rows of collector_budget_config; table CHECK constraints in migration 0004 bound each column. The code comment ties the 25 to the 50-subrequest Free limit. 4 statements are reserved for the keyword reindex batch.

facts.label: How the budgets are enforced
facts.value: budgetedFetch counts every external request and cancels a response that passes the byte limit; statementBudget counts every D1 statement and refuses a batch larger than what is left.
facts.how_counted: budgetedFetch() throws code BUDGET at the limit and boundedBody() aborts the reader past the byte limit. statementBudget().batch() returns false when sqlArgs.length > left. tests/collector.test.mjs "collector batches stop within the configured D1 query ceiling".

facts.label: Page checkpoint and postings in one batch
facts.how_counted: The same D1 batch writes the stored postings, the observations and the source_schedule checkpoint, so a cursor never advances past rows that were not stored. Test: "large complete board work resumes from a committed checkpoint until terminal".

facts.label: A failing source backs off alone
facts.how_counted: runCollector wraps each sourcePage() in try/catch; on error it writes failure_count, backoff_until and last_result for that source only and continues the loop. Backoff is 30 seconds doubled per failure, capped at 6 hours, or the provider Retry-After. Test: "an unexpected error in one source backs that source off and the run continues".

facts.label: Complete cycles of absence before a posting closes
facts.how_counted: posting_observations.missing_complete_cycles increments only when a board cycle ends terminal, complete and non-empty; closure needs >= 2. A reappearance resets it to 0. Tests: "an empty or failed board closes nothing", "repeated provider page is malformed and cannot count as evidence of closure".

facts.label: No description-less stub is stored
facts.how_counted: For providers that fetch one request per description (Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters) the loop cuts the page before the first job it has no request budget for. Test: five jobs, request_budget=3, asserts every stored row has a description and all five arrive over later runs.

facts.label: Closed postings are deleted after 30 days
facts.how_counted: PRUNE_DAYS = 30; DELETE ... WHERE open=0 AND embedded=0 and last observation older than the cutoff, LIMIT 100 per run. Child rows cascade; the FTS table has a delete trigger. Test: "postings closed for more than 30 days are deleted with their child rows".

facts.label: Posting identity
facts.value: Provider ID plus canonical HTTPS URL. A URL change is kept in posting_url_aliases; a changed source fingerprint writes posting_revisions; unchanged postings are not rewritten.
facts.how_counted: COLLECTOR_RULES rule 3 and docs/JOB-DATA-BOTS.md rule 5; posting_url_aliases and posting_revisions in migration 0004; tests "a second due cycle does not rewrite unchanged posting or normalization material" and "changed material keeps revisions and URL aliases while same-title locations stay distinct".

facts.label: Candidate shortlist
facts.how_counted: KEYWORD_ROWS = 1000 behind an FTS5 MATCH (tokenizer keeps underscores); up to 100 Vectorize neighbours; finder-pool.js TTL = 8 hours; collector VECTOR_CAP = 12000. Documented in docs/MATCHING-METHODOLOGY.md; the 100 semantic rows are from that document and were not re-derived from code.

facts.label: Requirements and evidence per assessment
facts.how_counted: postingRequirements(text, max=8) and prepareMatchEvidence(hits.slice(0,4)) in lib/match-evidence.js; MAX_JEV = 10 in lib/finder.js:18; per-click 50 is stated in SEARCH_RULES rule 10 (lib/finder.js:120).

facts.label: Fit score is computed in code
facts.value: relevance unrelated = 0; eligibility conflict = 1; coverage strong = 4, partial = 3, otherwise 2; unknown relevance caps at 2.
facts.how_counted: matchDetail() in lib/match-evidence.js. Coverage is recomputed from the per-requirement classifications and overrides the model's global answer. A positive classification without a cited source is downgraded to unknown; capability_gap requires negation wording in the cited excerpt. GPA is compared numerically in code.

facts.label: Question types sent to the model
facts.value: boolean, choice or score; yes counts at a threshold of 0.6 to 0.8 depending on the call; scores are clamped to 0-4; unknown choices fall back to a safe default.
facts.how_counted: docs/JEV-RULES.md design section and call table; tests/jev-safety.test.mjs (7 tests). Thresholds read from the docs table, not re-derived from every call site.

facts.label: Phrase patterns in the injection check
facts.how_counted: INSTRUCTION_PATTERNS array length. The file comment and JEV-RULES.md say it is a fixed phrase list that a reworded attack can get past; the fence and the closed answer types still apply.

facts.label: What the assessment cache stores
facts.value: Allowlisted choices, scores and source IDs under account, candidate, posting and rubric fingerprints. No resume or posting prose.
facts.how_counted: docs/JEV-RULES.md Known limits; docs/MATCHING-METHODOLOGY.md. Not re-derived from the cache code.

facts.label: Tenant isolation tests and responses
facts.how_counted: grep -c "^test(" in tests/scoping.test.mjs and tests/middleware.test.mjs. scoping.test.mjs seeds two accounts, then asserts each sees only its own jobs, notes, meta, extras and resumes and that a foreign row id returns 404 and leaves the row unchanged. _middleware.js returns 403 on an Origin mismatch and 401 without a session.

facts.label: Per-account keys
facts.value: meta, seen, job_extras, plan_tasks and calendar_accounts use a composite primary key that starts with user_id.
facts.how_counted: schema.sql lines 13, 16, 27, 35 and 44.

facts.label: Daily D1 allowance gate
facts.how_counted: READ_LIMIT, WRITE_LIMIT, READ_RESERVATION and WRITE_RESERVATION in lib/d1-budget.js. A Durable Object holds the counter; the raw D1 bindings live only in the gate Worker. Each call reserves first, persists the reservation, runs the SQL, then replaces the reservation with the measured rows. Missing or unmeasured results lock the day. docs/D1-BUDGET-GUARD.md says this is an application circuit breaker, not an account-wide cap.

facts.label: Gate tests
facts.how_counted: grep -c "^test(" in tests/d1-budget.test.mjs and tests/d1-client.test.mjs.

facts.label: What each timer does
facts.value: Every eight hours: runCollector. Daily 10:40 UTC: runFinder for account 1 plus pruneExpired. The employer-discovery timer is defined in code but not in wrangler.toml.
facts.how_counted: worker/index.js:10-19 and worker/wrangler.toml crons. docs/JOB-DATA-BOTS.md still says a 5-minute heartbeat and README.md says a 4-hour timer; both disagree with wrangler.toml, which is used here.

facts.label: Migrations
facts.value: Numbered SQL files per database. The collector migration is written to be safe to reapply; keyword taxonomy changes are refiled by a versioned cursor, 250 rows per run; the FTS index is backfilled separately in bounded ID ranges.
facts.how_counted: migrations-job-data/0004 header comment; KEYWORD_VERSION = 2 and the bot_rules cursor in lib/collector.js:432-450; 0009 header comment. Migration files 0007 and 0008 are data seeds without IF NOT EXISTS.

facts.label: How the tests run offline
facts.value: tests/d1.mjs wraps node:sqlite in memory and runs the real schema.sql and migrations-job-data files; provider fetch and the D1 gate are stubbed in the tests.
facts.how_counted: tests/d1.mjs makeDB(); tests/helpers.mjs migratedEnv(). Per-file counts by grep -c "^test(": collector 29, scoping 8, jev-safety 7, match-evidence 13.
